home.meta.title: glyphfox: icons that move, morph and fuse
home.meta.description: Original open source icons with variable weight, corners and style, a morph engine, fusion, modifiers and living states. React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, web components, Tailwind and a CLI.
home.meta.og: Variable, morphable and fusable open source icons with a studio in the browser.
home.hero.lead: Original icons on a 24 grid with variable weight, corners and style, a morph engine, fusion, modifier badges and living states. The same props in React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, web components, Tailwind and the CLI.
home.install.label: Install command
home.stats.label: glyphfox in numbers
home.axes.title: One icon. Every weight.
home.axes.lead: Every icon renders along three axes: weight from 1 to 3 with optical compensation at small sizes, round or sharp corners, and outline, duotone or solid style generated from its closed shapes.
home.play.title: Dial it in.
home.play.lead: Drag the sliders. Every component in every framework takes the same props.
home.morph.title: Anything into anything.
home.morph.lead: Paths are normalized, resampled, matched and interpolated, so any icon turns into any other. Hand tuned pairs make the everyday ones feel designed.
home.living.title: Icons that know how to move.
home.living.lead: Presets that understand the icon: draw traces the strokes in order, shake swings from the top like a bell. Trigger them on mount, hover, click or a state prop. Reduced motion is always respected.
home.mods.title: Badges that cut their own gap.
home.mods.lead: Add plus, check, alert, lock, clock, sync and more in any corner. The icon underneath is trimmed around the badge, so a few hundred icons give thousands of clean combinations.
home.mp.title: Modifier playground
home.fusion.title: Two icons. One new glyph.
home.fusion.lead: Fuse 2 to 10 icons with seven layouts. Parts are scaled and snapped to the grid, and where they overlap the one behind is cut around the one in front, so lines never collide and the result still passes the lint.
home.gallery.title: New icons, already in the set.
home.studio.title: A whole icon workshop in your browser.
home.studio.lead: No account, no server. Everything runs on your machine and your collection stays in your browser.
home.film.title: glyphfox 1.0 in two and a half minutes.
home.film.lead: Every icon, scene and sound in it was made with code.

docs.meta.title: Docs: glyphfox
docs.meta.description: Install glyphfox and use it with React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, the web component, the CDN, Tailwind CSS, plain HTML and the CLI. Every prop, the name syntax, morph, fusion, living states and modifiers.
docs.title: Everything glyphfox can do
docs.lead: One set of props in every framework. Learn the install, each package, the name syntax and the engines behind morph, fusion and living states.
docs.install.p: glyphfox has no dependencies. React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact, Qwik, Lit, Astro, React Native, Ember and Tailwind CSS are optional peer dependencies, used only when you import their entry points.
docs.react.p: Each icon is a tree shakable forwardRef component named after the icon: arrow-right becomes ArrowRightIcon. className, style and every SVG attribute pass through to the svg.
docs.react.p2: useMorph(name, options) returns icon data that morphs whenever the name changes, for custom renderers. registerIcons(icons) makes names available synchronously, for example during server rendering.
docs.vue.p: Props use the same names; in templates you can also write them in kebab-case (secondary-color). The useMorph(nameRef) composable mirrors the React hook.
docs.svelte.p: For Svelte 5. Components ship as .svelte files compiled by your app. morphStore(name) is a store that morphs on every set(name).
docs.angular.p: glyphfox-angular is published in the Angular package format, built with ng-packagr. GlyphFoxIcon is a standalone component; provideGlyphFox registers icons by name and default props.
docs.web.p: One file with every icon, the element and the plain HTML runtime. Every prop is an attribute in kebab-case. With a bundler, import glyphfox/web, or glyphfox/web/element to register only your icons. The morph attribute animates every change of name.
docs.tailwind.p: Icons render as CSS masks in currentColor, so color, size and opacity utilities apply. After the slash you can join axes, a fusion layout or a badge corner with dashes. Tailwind v4 only accepts + and & inside brackets; v3 also accepts gf-file+check.
docs.html.p: The runtime swaps every element with data-glyph for inline SVG, including elements added later. Props are data attributes in kebab-case.
docs.js.p: The package also ships icons.json, sprite.svg, styles.css, glyphfox/core (the engine without icon data) and glyphfox/tools (lint and Fox-ify).
docs.props.p: The same props, names and meaning in React, Vue, Svelte, Angular, the web component and toSvg. Plus class and style, passed to the svg (or to the host element for Angular and the web component).
prop.size: Width and height; numbers are pixels.
prop.secondaryColor: Color of the duotone layer and of the solid fill.
prop.secondaryOpacity: Opacity of the duotone layer or of the solid fill.
prop.weight: Stroke from 1 to 3 on the 24 grid, optically compensated below 24 px.
prop.absoluteWeight: Keeps the stroke at weight pixels at any size.
prop.corners: Round or sharp joins and caps.
prop.variant: Style axis; solid comes from the closed shapes.
prop.mirrorRtl: Mirror in right to left layouts.
prop.trigger: When the animation or the morph plays.
prop.loop: Repeat forever or a number of times (spin and pulse loop by default).
prop.modifier: Badge with an automatic knockout gap.
prop.morphTo: Morph target; the trigger decides when it shows.
prop.title: Accessible name: title, role img and aria-label.
prop.decorative: Hides the icon from assistive technology.
docs.syntax.p: Shared by the web component, the CDN, Tailwind, the CLI, the Icon component and toSvg.
syntax.corner: badge in a corner: tl, tr, bl, br
docs.axes.p: Weight runs from 1 to 3. Below 24 px the stroke grows a little so small icons keep their presence; absoluteWeight turns this off. Corners switch between round and sharp joins and caps. The solid style fills the closed outer shapes and cuts the inner lines out as negative space; it is computed at build time for the set and at render time for fusions and modifiers.
docs.morph.p: Paths are flattened into strands, matched with an optimal assignment, resampled to the same number of points, aligned and interpolated. Strands without a partner shrink and fade. Hand tuned hints cover the common pairs. Without JavaScript, toSvg with morphTo returns an SVG that morphs with a CSS d transition and cross fades where that is not supported.
docs.fusion.p: fuse combines 2 to 10 icons into one icon that still passes the lint. Layouts: overlap, side, stack, grid (2x2, 3x3 and 10 slots), orbit, badge and inside. Parts are scaled and snapped to the grid, and the part behind is trimmed around the part in front with a knockout gap. Options: layout, gap, weight, scale and offsets.
docs.living.p: Each preset is a small stylesheet inside the SVG, so it works everywhere the SVG goes. draw traces the strokes in drawing order, shake swings from the top. Triggers: mount, hover (the icon or its direct parent), click (replays on each click) and state (plays while active). Reduced motion turns every animation off.
docs.mods.p: Eleven badges in four corners. The icon underneath is trimmed around the badge geometrically, so the result is a plain icon that passes the lint, in every weight.
docs.cli.p: copy prints the snippet and puts it on the clipboard (formats: svg, jsx, vue, svelte, angular, html, tailwind, cdn, datauri). build makes a sprite, a CSS file with mask classes or a small package from a list. Every command takes the shared props as flags, such as --weight 1.5 --corners sharp.
docs.rules.p: Original drawings only, on a 24 by 24 grid: viewBox 0 0 24 24, no fill, stroke currentColor, stroke width 2, round caps and joins, 2 px padding, no transforms, and no fills except one optional duotone layer with the class gf-secondary. Sources live in icons/NAME.svg with a NAME.json sidecar for categories and tags, and tools/icons/lint.mjs checks them.
docs.social.p: The social category holds brand icons for the networks people link to most, from Instagram, WhatsApp, Facebook, X, TikTok and YouTube to GitHub, Discord, Spotify and Steam. Each one is named brand-NAME, drawn as an outline of the logo on the same grid and stroke as the rest of the set, and tagged with the network name, its old names, social, logo and brand.
docs.collections.p: Two signature collections ship with the package next to the base set: display, 60 icons drawn on a 48 grid for empty states, onboarding and large tiles, and isometric, 30 icons in isometric projection on the 24 grid. Write their names as display/NAME and isometric/NAME in toSvg, the web component, the CDN build and the Icon component. Their data comes from glyphfox/collections, and the React, Vue and Svelte components from glyphfox/react/collections, glyphfox/vue/collections and glyphfox/svelte/collections, so the default entries stay as small as before.
docs.collections.limits: Size, color, weight, rotation, flips and the animation presets work on both. Display icons default to 48 px and measure weight in units of their 48 grid, so weight 2 keeps the drawn stroke. The solid and duotone styles, modifier badges, fusion and morphs are cut for the 24 grid: display icons stay outline, and a fusion or a modifier spec with one of them is an error. Isometric icons support every feature of the base set.
docs.social.tm: Brand icons are trademarks of their owners and must be used under each brand's guidelines.

native.meta.title: Native exports: glyphfox
native.meta.description: Export glyphfox icons as Android VectorDrawable XML, Jetpack Compose ImageVector code, an iOS asset catalog with SwiftUI helpers, and Flutter SVG assets with a Dart constants file and a GlyphFoxIcon widget.
native.hero.title: Native exports
native.hero.lead: One command turns glyphfox icons into real vector assets for Android, Jetpack Compose, iOS, SwiftUI and Flutter. Weight, corners, duotone, modifiers and fusions export as plain paths, and strokes stay strokes.
native.overview.p: Pass icon names or any spec of the name syntax, a list file with --from (one name per line, # starts a comment) or --all for the whole set. The geometry is the one the web packages draw, so the same specs look the same everywhere:
native.android.p: One VectorDrawable per icon in drawable/, so point --out at app/src/main/res. Strokes keep their width in viewport units, their round or square caps and joins, and never get a fill, so they scale with the drawable exactly like the SVG. The color is a tint: ?attr/colorControlNormal by default, so the icons follow the theme like the Material icons do.
native.android.color: Pass a theme attribute or a color resource as --color (?attr/colorPrimary, @color/brand) to tint with it, or a hex color (#ff7a1a) to bake the color into the paths without a tint. Duotone layers are filled paths with fillAlpha, --mirror-rtl sets android:autoMirrored, and rotate and flips become a group around the center.
native.compose.p: GlyphFox.kt declares the GlyphFox object and every icon is an ImageVector extension property on it, built on first use and cached, in its own file. The files go to the package folder under --out, so point it at the Kotlin source root.
native.compose.names: Each property is imported by name, like the Material icons. GlyphFox.all maps every exported name to its vector for pickers and previews. With code shrinking on, R8 removes the icons an app never uses, unless it reads GlyphFox.all.
native.ios.p: One image set per icon with the SVG, Preserve Vector Data and Render As Template Image, so the icons stay sharp at any size and take the tint color. Point --out at an existing catalog such as MyApp/Assets.xcassets to add the image sets to it (its own Contents.json is kept), or at a folder to get GlyphFox.xcassets.
native.ios.color: The SVG files carry concrete colors (black by default), which template rendering replaces with the tint. With a hex --color the catalog switches to original rendering so the color shows; --rendering template or original picks one explicitly, and --mirror-rtl marks the image sets to flip in right to left layouts.
native.swiftui.p: glyphfox export swiftui writes the same asset catalog plus GlyphFox.swift: an enum with one case per image set, Image(glyphfox:) and UIImage.glyphfox(_:) for UIKit.
native.swiftui.bundle: Pass bundle: .module when the catalog lives in a Swift package.
native.flutter.p: SVG files in assets/glyphfox/ and lib/glyphfox.dart with one constant per icon and a small GlyphFoxIcon widget on top of flutter_svg. Point --out at the app folder, then add the package and the assets to pubspec.yaml:
native.flutter.widget: GlyphFoxIcon follows the surrounding IconTheme for size and color like Icon does, tints the whole drawing (the duotone layer keeps its opacity) and is decorative unless it gets a semanticLabel. GlyphFoxIcons.values lists every exported path, and --assets moves the SVG folder.
native.opt.specs: Names or specs such as file+check@tr, cloud&lock:side or heart/duotone.
native.opt.from: A list file: one name per line or separated by commas, # starts a comment.
native.opt.out: The project folder: res for android, the Kotlin source root for compose, a folder or an .xcassets catalog for ios and swiftui, the app folder for flutter.
native.opt.size: Size in dp, points or logical pixels. Below 24 the stroke is optically compensated, as on the web.
native.opt.weight: Stroke width from 1 to 3 on the 24 grid.
native.opt.absoluteWeight: Keeps the stroke at weight units at the export size.
native.opt.variant: outline or duotone. The solid style cuts lines out with masks, which VectorDrawable and ImageVector cannot draw, so it is refused.
native.opt.color: A hex color baked into the files. Android also takes a theme attribute or a color resource, used as the tint.
native.opt.secondary: Color and opacity of the duotone layer.
native.opt.transform: A transform around the center of the grid.
native.opt.mirror: Flips the icon in right to left layouts (autoMirrored, autoMirror, the image set direction).
native.opt.modifier: The same badge on every icon, like file+check.
native.opt.prefix: Prefix of the drawable or image set names.
native.opt.package: Kotlin package, also the folder under --out.
native.opt.rendering: template or original; original is the default with a hex --color.
native.opt.assets: Folder of the SVG files and of the paths in the constants.
native.names.p: A spec becomes a name on each platform: file+check@tr is gf_file_check_tr on Android, GlyphFox.FileCheckTr in Compose, gf-file-check-tr in the catalog and fileCheckTr in Swift and Dart. Two specs that end up with the same name are refused, and keywords are escaped (repeat becomes `repeat` in Swift).
native.names.color: Without --color every target follows the platform tint: colorControlNormal, LocalContentColor, the SwiftUI foreground style or IconTheme. With a hex color the color is baked in and stays: Android drops the tint, the catalog renders the original and GlyphFoxIcon keeps the exported colors unless it gets a color. Compose Icon() always tints, so use Image() or tint = Color.Unspecified to see the baked color.
smart.meta.title: Smart icons: glyphfox
smart.meta.description: glyphfox smart icons: battery, signal, wifi, volume, progress, thermometer, calendar, clock, file and badge icons drawn from data, currency from the locale, automatic right to left mirroring, a contrast weight bump, a morphing StatusIcon and staggered IconGroup animations.
smart.hero.title: Icons that show data, follow the reader and report status
smart.hero.lead: Battery, signal, wifi, volume, progress, thermometer, calendar, clock, file and badge icons drawn from a value, a date or a count. A currency sign that comes from the locale, arrows that turn around in right to left layouts and lines that get heavier when the reader asks for more contrast. A status icon that morphs from loading to done, and groups that animate in a wave.
smart.data.p: Every data icon is drawn on the same 24 grid, with the same stroke, caps and padding as the rest of the set, so size, color, weight, corners, variant, animate and title work as usual. The value runs from 0 to 1. A value above 1 without a max is read as a percentage, and min with max map real values, such as a temperature.
smart.data.classes: Each icon carries classes for its state (gf-low, gf-full, gf-charging, gf-muted, gf-hot, gf-cold), and unlit bars and arcs carry gf-off, so a stylesheet can color them. title="auto" gives the icon an accessible name that describes the data, such as "Battery 64%", with numbers formatted for the locale.
smart.time.p: The calendar shows today by default, or the date you pass (a Date, a timestamp or "2026-10-23"), with the digits of the locale. The clock shows the current time, or a given time ("09:30", "18:45:10" or a Date); seconds adds the second hand. With tick, the clock and the calendar follow the real time, updating once per second, per minute or at midnight.
smart.files.p: The file icon prints its extension (up to four letters) from ext or a filename. The badge puts a notification count on the bell, or on any icon given as icon, with the same knockout gap the modifiers use. Counts above max (99) read "99+", 0 hides the bubble and dot shows a dot. badgeColor colors the bubble; the number is cut out of it, so it reads on any background.
smart.currency.p: kind="currency" picks its sign from the locale: the region gives the currency and Intl.NumberFormat gives its symbol, which is drawn as R$, the euro, the yen (also for the yuan), the pound, the dollar (also for pesos and other dollars) or the generic currency sign. Pass currency="EUR" to choose the currency yourself. Without a locale, the icon uses the language of the document, then the language of the browser.
smart.rtl.p: Directional icons (arrows, chevrons, undo and redo, reply, send, log in and out, lists, indent) now mirror by themselves in right to left layouts, in every package: they carry the gf-rtl class and a rule that flips them under dir="rtl". With a locale or dir prop the decision follows that locale instead of the page, so an Arabic widget in an English page still points the right way. mirrorRtl={false} turns it off, and registerDirectional(['my-arrow']) adds your own icons. Media controls such as play and fast forward never mirror.
smart.contrast.p: When the reader asks for more contrast (prefers-contrast: more), smart icons draw their lines half a weight step heavier, set their labels bolder and raise the unlit parts. The rule travels inside the SVG, so it also works in server rendered markup and in exported files. contrast="more" applies the bump all the time and contrast="off" never does.
smart.status.p: One icon for the four states of a task: idle, loading, success and error. Every change morphs with the glyphfox morph engine (the circle opens into the spinner, the spinner closes around the check), and loading spins once the morph has settled. duration times the morph, spinDuration the spin, and reduced motion jumps straight to the new state.
smart.status.css: Without JavaScript, statusSvg('success', { from: 'loading' }) returns an SVG that morphs on load with CSS only.
smart.group.p: A group plays one living state preset across its icons with a stagger between them. Triggers: mount, hover (the whole group), click (replays on every click) and state (plays while active). from="end" or "center" changes the order of the wave. Children that set their own preset or delay keep it; icons renders names, icon data or smart items for you.
smart.packages.p: The same three pieces ship in React, Vue and Svelte (SmartIcon, StatusIcon, IconGroup), as custom elements and as plain functions in the core.
smart.packages.data: smartIcon(kind, options) returns plain icon data, so a smart icon can also feed renderIcon, a custom renderer or the morph engine. In glyphfox/core the same functions resolve names from the icons you register.
smart.options.p: On top of every shared prop. Attributes use kebab-case (badge-color).
smart.options.kind: battery, signal, wifi, volume, progress, thermometer, calendar, clock, file, badge or currency. Without a kind, name renders any icon with the locale and contrast behaviors.
smart.options.value: The level: 0 to 1, a percentage, or a real value between min and max.
smart.options.charging: Draws a bolt cut into the level.
smart.options.label: true prints the percentage inside the ring, a string prints up to four characters.
smart.options.unit: Unit of the accessible description, such as "°C".
smart.options.date: A Date, a timestamp or "YYYY-MM-DD". Default today.
smart.options.time: "HH:MM", "HH:MM:SS", a Date or { hours, minutes }. Default now. seconds adds the second hand.
smart.options.tick: Follows the real time (when no time or date is given).
smart.options.ext: The extension label, up to four characters.
smart.options.count: The count, the largest number shown before "+" (99) and a dot instead of a number.
smart.options.icon: The icon under the bubble (default bell) and the color of the bubble.
smart.options.currency: An ISO code instead of the currency of the locale.
smart.options.locale: Symbols, digits and dates; also decides the mirroring of directional icons.
smart.options.contrast: auto (default) follows prefers-contrast: more, more always bumps the weight, off never does.
smart.options.title: An accessible name that describes the data or the state.
smart.options.state: idle, loading, success or error; the length of one turn of the spin.
smart.options.group: The preset, the delay between icons (60 ms), the first delay, the order of the wave, the trigger, the state and the icons to render.
frameworks.meta.title: Frameworks: glyphfox
frameworks.meta.description: glyphfox in every framework: React, React Server Components, Vue, Svelte, Angular, Solid, Preact, Qwik, Lit, Astro, React Native, Ember, the web component and Tailwind CSS, plus recipes for Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, Remix, Alpine and htmx.
frameworks.nav.title: On this page
frameworks.hero.title: One icon set, every framework
frameworks.hero.lead: Every package takes the same props (size, color, weight, corners, variant, animate, modifier, morphTo and the rest) and renders the same SVG. Pick your framework, or follow a recipe for your meta framework.
frameworks.packages.p: Everything ships in the glyphfox package (Angular also has glyphfox-angular). Each framework is an optional peer dependency, used only when you import its entry point. Icon components are tree shakable and every entry point is typed.
frameworks.table.rsc: Hook free Icon and Fusion, zero JavaScript
frameworks.table.preact: Components and hooks, no compat layer
frameworks.table.qwik: Lightweight components that resume with no JavaScript
frameworks.solid.p: No JSX compiler setup and no special export condition: the same module renders in SolidStart on the server and in the browser. class, style, ref and events pass through to the svg. useMorph(accessor) returns an accessor of icon data that morphs whenever the name changes.
frameworks.preact.p: The same API as React (Icon, Fusion, MorphIcon, useMorph) built on preact and preact/hooks, so it does not pull in preact/compat. On Preact 11 a ref reaches the svg element. Both class and className work.
frameworks.qwik.p: Built for Qwik 2 (@qwik.dev/core). The icons are lightweight components: they render on the server and resume without downloading anything. Living states and morphTo run on CSS, active switches trigger="state", and trigger="click" uses a tiny inline handler. Names used by Icon, morphTo and Fusion must be registered: icon components register their icon, and registerIcons([iconX]) (or registerIcons(icons) with icons from glyphfox for the whole set) covers names you only write as strings.
frameworks.lit.p: Nothing is registered on import: defineIcons(list, { prefix }) defines the elements you use ({ prefix: 'my' } gives <my-file>). Attributes are kebab-case (secondary-color, flip-x, morph-to), properties camelCase; the animate attribute is the animatePreset property, because animate() is a method of every element, and animation plays the designed animation as in every package. class and style style the host element. The elements render in shadow DOM and work with @lit-labs/ssr.
frameworks.astro.p: Components render static SVG on the server and ship no JavaScript. Every icon of the set is available to Icon names, morphTo and Fusion. class (and class:list), style as a string or an object, and any other attribute pass through to the svg. Hover, mount and state triggers run on CSS; trigger="click" uses a tiny inline handler.
frameworks.native.p: Components render react-native-svg elements with the same props. There is no CSS on native, so living states are sampled frame by frame from the same presets and morphs are tweened; both follow the reduce motion setting. trigger="click" plays on press and trigger="hover" while pressed. title sets the accessibility label, style and other props reach the Svg, and refs are forwarded. Metro resolves the glyphfox/native export with package exports, on by default since React Native 0.79.
frameworks.ember.p: Plain function helpers (Ember 4.5 and newer), so they need no addon setup and work in .gjs, .gts and classic templates. They return trusted markup: the shared props, class, style and other attributes are named arguments. Names used by Glyph, morphTo and Fusion must be registered: icon helpers register their icon, and registerIcons([iconCloud]) (or registerIcons(icons)) covers the rest. Hover, mount and state triggers run on CSS; trigger="click" uses a tiny inline handler.
recipes.nextjs.meta.title: Next.js App Router: glyphfox
recipes.nextjs.meta.description: Use glyphfox icons in the Next.js App Router: zero JavaScript Server Components with glyphfox/react/server, interactive client components with glyphfox/react, tree shaking and the sprite.
recipes.nextjs.server.title: Server Components
recipes.nextjs.client.title: Client components
recipes.nextjs.bundle.title: Bundle size
recipes.nextjs.title: Next.js App Router with Server Components
recipes.nextjs.lead: Render icons in Server Components with no JavaScript at all, and reach for client components only where an icon reacts to clicks or morphs between names.
recipes.nextjs.server.p: glyphfox/react/server exports hook free Icon and Fusion components. They render static SVG during the server render, so nothing is sent to the browser for them, and every icon of the set is available by name. Living states, hover and state morphs travel inside the SVG as CSS.
recipes.nextjs.client.p: The modules of glyphfox/react are marked 'use client', so the icon components also work when a Server Component renders them directly: they are server rendered and hydrated. Use them where you need the click trigger, morph tweens or useMorph.
recipes.nextjs.bundle.p: Each icon is its own module. With optimizePackageImports Next.js rewrites barrel imports to those modules; deep imports such as import { FileIcon } from 'glyphfox/react/icons/file' work everywhere without configuration.
recipes.nextjs.sprite.p: For long lists of static icons, a sprite of just the icons you use keeps the HTML small and caches across pages.
recipes.nuxt.meta.title: Nuxt: glyphfox
recipes.nuxt.meta.description: Use glyphfox icons in Nuxt: explicit imports, auto imported components with a local module, server rendering and Tailwind CSS.
recipes.nuxt.imports.title: Explicit imports
recipes.nuxt.auto.title: Auto imported components
recipes.nuxt.lead: glyphfox/vue renders on the server and hydrates in the browser, so icons work in Nuxt pages, layouts and components without extra build configuration.
recipes.nuxt.imports.p: Explicit imports keep only the icons you use in the bundle, and need no Nuxt configuration. build.transpile is not needed: the package ships plain ESM.
recipes.nuxt.auto.p: A small local module (files in modules/ load automatically) registers the components you choose, so templates can use <HomeIcon /> without an import and Nuxt still adds only the ones a page uses.
recipes.nuxt.ssr.p: Icon components register themselves. Names that only appear as strings, in <Icon name="cloud" />, morphTo or Fusion, load on demand in the browser; register them in a plugin so the server render already contains them.
recipes.nuxt.tailwind.p: With the Tailwind plugin, <span class="gf-home size-5 text-orange-500"></span> draws an icon as a CSS mask, which suits long static lists.
recipes.remix.meta.title: Remix and React Router: glyphfox
recipes.remix.meta.description: Use glyphfox icons in Remix and React Router framework mode: server rendered components, names during server rendering and a cached sprite through links.
recipes.remix.routes.title: Routes
recipes.remix.sprite.title: A cached sprite
recipes.remix.lead: glyphfox/react renders on the server and hydrates in the browser, so it works in Remix and in React Router framework mode (the successor of Remix) without configuration.
recipes.remix.routes.p: Components are server rendered with the route and hydrate with it. Imports stay tree shakable with the Vite build.
recipes.remix.names.p: Icon components register themselves. Register icons you only reference by name (<Icon name="cloud" />, morphTo, Fusion) so the server render contains them.
recipes.remix.sprite.p: The full sprite is a single cached file. For production, npx glyphfox build --type sprite makes one with only the icons you use.
recipes.sveltekit.meta.title: SvelteKit: glyphfox
recipes.sveltekit.meta.description: Use glyphfox icons in SvelteKit: Svelte 5 components compiled by your app, server rendering, prerendering, deep imports and the morph store.
recipes.sveltekit.page.title: Pages and components
recipes.sveltekit.deep.title: Deep imports
recipes.sveltekit.prerender.title: Prerendering and names
recipes.sveltekit.morph.title: Morph store
recipes.sveltekit.lead: glyphfox/svelte ships .svelte sources that SvelteKit compiles with the rest of your app, so icons render on the server, prerender to static HTML and hydrate.
recipes.sveltekit.page.p: No Vite configuration is needed: the package exposes the svelte export condition, which SvelteKit resolves for server and client builds.
recipes.sveltekit.deep.p: Each icon is also its own component file, which keeps development servers fast in large apps.
recipes.sveltekit.prerender.p: Prerendered pages contain the full SVG markup. Register the icons you only reference by name (<Icon name="cloud" />, morphTo, Fusion) so they are part of the server render instead of loading in the browser.
recipes.alpine.meta.title: Alpine.js: glyphfox
recipes.alpine.meta.description: Use glyphfox icons with Alpine.js: the glyph-fox web component bound with x-bind, morphs on name changes, state triggers and x-html with the CDN build.
recipes.alpine.setup.title: Setup
recipes.alpine.bind.title: Bind props
recipes.alpine.html.title: Inline SVG with x-html
recipes.alpine.lead: The <glyph-fox> web component reacts to attribute changes, which is exactly what Alpine bindings produce. No build step needed.
recipes.alpine.setup.p: The glyphfox CDN build defines <glyph-fox> with every icon and exposes window.glyphfox.
recipes.alpine.bind.p: With the morph attribute, every change of name animates from the old icon to the new one. Every prop is an attribute in kebab-case, so :weight, :modifier and :morph-to bind the same way.
recipes.alpine.html.p: glyphfox.toSvg returns plain SVG markup with the same props, for places where a custom element does not fit, such as inside an existing svg.
recipes.htmx.meta.title: htmx: glyphfox
recipes.htmx.meta.description: Use glyphfox icons with htmx: server rendered SVG fragments with toSvg, glyph-fox elements in swapped content and the data-glyph runtime.
recipes.htmx.server.title: Render SVG on the server
recipes.htmx.elements.title: Web components in swapped content
recipes.htmx.runtime.title: The data-glyph runtime
recipes.htmx.lead: htmx swaps HTML from the server, and every glyphfox format is HTML: inline SVG rendered on the server, <glyph-fox> elements, or data-glyph placeholders.
recipes.htmx.server.p: toSvg returns the icon as markup with every prop, and the animation styles travel inside it, so the swapped fragment plays the pop as soon as it lands. Any Node server or edge function works the same way.
recipes.htmx.elements.p: Custom elements upgrade by themselves when htmx inserts them, so fragments can return <glyph-fox> tags. With a swap that keeps elements and updates their attributes, such as the idiomorph extension, a <glyph-fox morph> element animates when the server changes its name.
recipes.htmx.runtime.p: The runtime replaces every data-glyph element with inline SVG and keeps watching, so placeholders in swapped content are replaced too. With a bundler, call replaceGlyphs after each swap instead.
